stop_conditions: Confirmed root cause: redis catalog TTL misconfiguration or eviction pattern explaining repeated product SQL.
All p95 latency under baseline thresholds for gateway, order-service, and inventory-service across two consecutive windows.
Two independent tools (e.g., inspect_redis and query_metrics) corroborate the same mechanism with no contradicting evidence.
Repeated retrieval yields no new evidence or contradictions across 3 or more tool calls.
initial_hypotheses: Inventory-service cache effectiveness degraded: catalog TTL of -2 suggests entries expire/nonexistent, causing repeated product SQL (SELECT id,name,price,stock FROM products) and elevated db churn.
Redis shared counter scope includes control traffic, muddying cache-hit signals and possibly masking a genuine cache-miss storm on product catalog reads.
Order-service checkout latency (avg ~30ms, p99 ~67ms) is dominated by downstream inventory/payment calls rather than local compute.
No HTTP errors observed across services, but cumulative pool wait on inventory-service (525760ms waits, 441 errors) indicates historical queue/pool pressure not visible in current gauges.
